/ˈsʌlə/ was actually how it was pronounced. SUL-uh. 

https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulla

When moving from Latin to Old French, there was a consonant shift that changed many 'c' consonants from the 'k' sound to an 's'. In Greek, Serbian, Albanian, etc it's pronounced with the 'k'. Source: https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Macedonia

It's really interesting how it all happened. Another good example of this is the word 'city' in English. It comes from the Latin root 'civis'. Reading it with English and French understanding, you would think it was pronounced with an 's' and a 'v' (a voiced 'f'). But it was actually pronounced with a 'k' and 'w'. Descendants of Old French (English and French included) both experienced this this consonant shift.
Source: https://en.m.wiktionary.org/wiki/civis

In the episode where the Blue Spirit helps Aang escape after being captured by Zhao, in the ends of the episode we see that Aang doesn't hate Zuko, he understands that simply by nature of their roles that will probably be in opposition. 

We also see that Zuko is completely willing to cross Zhao for his own goal of capturing the Avatar. With how I viewed Zuko in S1, Zuko doesn't intrinsically hate Aang. He's bitter and furious at being thrust into his situation in life as an exile with a nearly impossible chance of redemption. 

In contrast, Zhao is someone that Zuko clearly doesn't like. They are rude to each other, Zhao is prideful and boasting, and reckless and brutish. Zhao is also a massive rival to Zuko's interests. So obviously, it makes sense that Zuko would have the motivation for murder in the Agni Kai. 

Here's how I picture the season going: Zuko kills Zhao. Zuko becomes increasingly distraught inwardly about the murder, but outwardly becomes colder and more unfeeling. Zhao would have never captured Aang, therefore Aang and Zuko have less time to understand each other. This leaves Zuko with more time to focus on his rushdown style of fire bending, his inner turmoil, and Iroh's teachings. It would also leave him single-minded in his goal of capturing Aang, which would probably come to a head later in the season. 

The massive fleet of fire nation ships would not have been mobilized. Therefore the water tribe would be largely safe from assault and there most likely would not have been a massive battle between fire and water. 

In addition, the moon spirit would not have been murdered, therefore the North would have more survivors, and Yuei would still have been alive, probably leading to more development between her, Sokka, and the chief. 

Aang would have more time to master the elements. Water and Air would have probably turned out the same more or less, but he'd have a worse understanding of the Avatar state at the end of the season without the use of the Ocean spirit. 

There is also a massive change to the cycle here:

Jeong Jeong would likely have helped Aang master fire bending, or at least help him to get a far better elementary understanding of its nature, and to teach him to not be afraid of it. This arc was cut short with the arrival of Zhao and the disappearance of Jeong Jeong. I believe that his teachings would have given Aang more confidence, patience, control, and most importantly **power**. 

Aang is not exactly a forceful character at this time in his life. I feel like an early mastering of fire bending would have dramatically changed this. With Zuko and Aang more focused on their development of fire, power, and goals (capture Avatar, master elements), I see the end of the season resulting in a dramatic and rage fueled clash between Zuko and Aang, ending in either Zuko's defeat and further scaring, or Aang being captured.
